      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya</link>
      <description><p>No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia</p><p>A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p>The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/monday-briefing-what-could-andy-burnhams-reset-mean-for-the-uk</link>
      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: The prime minister has reopened the debate over a future relationship with a changed EU – as the bloc faces the rise of the far right, a protectionist economic agenda and growing defence ambitions</p><p>Good morning. Nobody really wants to think about Brexit any more, save for the original Brexiters, who seem delighted that Andy Burnham’s “reset” with the EU has given them an excuse to get the old gang back together. But arguments about whether the UK should rejoin the EU will reignite in parliament this week, as Burnham briefs MPs on the deal he agreed on Friday.</p><p>That deal wasn’t so much a victory as the culmination of Keir Starmer’s incrementalist approach to UK-EU relations. Its core agreements haven’t been ratified by member states yet, and the EU won’t sign them off until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students. Burnham is apparently “determined” to take the UK back into the EU, but don’t expect any progress on that before the next general election.</p><p><em><strong>Cop</strong></em><em><strong>31 </strong></em>| The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/22/cop31-climate-talks-set-to-end-in-deep-division-as-key-deal-rejected">rejected what they called an unacceptable deal</a> that “failed to meet the moment” in a dramatic finish to the UN talks in Turkey. The proposed deal failed to endorse a away from fossil fuels that more than 130 countries demanded.</p><p><em><strong>Russia </strong></em>| A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in a suspected <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Ukrainian sea drone attack</a>, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p><em><strong>Weapons</strong></em>| The Red Cross and other rights groups <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/nov/22/red-cross-warns-too-late-regulate-autonomous-weapons-united-nations">have warned that it will soon</a> be too late to properly regulate the development of autonomous weapons. The warning came as the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons concluded without an agreement on an instrument for regulating autonomous weapons.</p><p><em><strong>UK news </strong></em>| Dozens of hospitals are so short of money they may not be able to continue caring for patients and are being forced to make “unpalatable” cuts to services and staff,<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/22/nhs-savings-hospitals-trusts-england-cuts"> the Guardian can reveal.</a></p><p><em><strong>West Bank </strong></em>| Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/netanyahu-rival-condemns-settler-arson-attacks-palestinian-villages-west-bank">condemned arson attacks</a> by militant Israeli settlers on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank after dozens of settlers raided Palestinian communities overnight on Saturday.</p><p><em><strong>Monday</strong></em> | FIFA is set to announce that the UK will host the 2035 Women’s World Cup.</p><p><em><strong>Thursday </strong></em>| RMT will begin a series of eight 24-hour strikes on the London Underground over the next three months due to a dispute over a four-day week for its drivers.</p><p><em><strong>Sunday</strong></em> | Spain will hold snap parliamentary elections in what will be the country’s sixth general election in 11 years.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/monday-briefing-what-could-andy-burnhams-reset-mean-for-the-uk">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Tories welcome Louise Haigh’s hint government could adopt their plan to scrap Natural England – UK politics live</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-brexit-europe-eu-uk-summit-deal-commons-cbi-farage-badenoch-haigh-politics-latest-news-updates</link>
      <description><p>First secretary of state has declined to say whether Natural England will be abolished as part of plans to cut the number of quangos</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/23/natural-england-could-be-abolished-quango-cull-louise-haigh">Natural England could be abolished as part of quango cull, says Louise Haigh</a></p></li></ul><p>In her speech to the CBI, <strong>Louise Haigh</strong>, the first secretary of state, delivered one of the most detailed explanations we have had from a minister as to what Andy Burnham means when he calls for more public control of utilities.</p><p>She said that the government was not against markets, and that in areas like telecoms privatisation had worked. But in water and energy it hadn’t, she insisted. She suggested that, in wanting more public control in these sectors, the government was aligned with the US, “hardly a hotbed of state socialism”.</p><p>Now I know the word privatisation can start an argument. So let me be precise. This is not about whether markets work. They do. Where there is genuine competition, as in telecoms, markets have given consumers choice and kept prices low while delivering infrastructure.</p><p>The social licence to operate must be won every day by building trust and having the best value, product or service. Where competition exists, it should be left to thrive, supported by our strong, independent Competition and Markets Authority.</p><p>To make the experiment work, successive governments leant on regulation, first to try to recreate competition from monopolies through a spreadsheet; then to manage what private markets would never price on their own, like the spare capacity that keeps the lights on; then to deliver social policy, treated as a free good because it went on the bill, not the budget.</p><p>Ofgem now has six times the staff it had in the early 2000s, almost three times the administrative budget in real terms, and a rule book more than six times longer. We’ve got a hulking, complex behemoth of a regulatory state. It satisfies no one. Not consumers, not investors. When you prioritise everything, you prioritise nothing.</p><p>We’ve set in place a process in order to protect our critical industries, including the automotive industry and steel, from the Made in Europe agenda.</p><p>And our message to Europe was that, on industry, they are worried about the Chinese flooding of products onto the market. We share that concern, and we share that challenge. So let’s work together. We don’t have to be competitors in that space; we benefit each other in the trading relationship.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-brexit-europe-eu-uk-summit-deal-commons-cbi-farage-badenoch-haigh-politics-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>
